tabela.afirmacao: On August 27, 1974, Alaska voters approved moving their state capital out of Juneau.
tabela.fonte_diz: Official Returns, primária de 27/08/1974: 'Initiative #1 - Relocating and Constructing A New Capital', FOR 46,659, AGAINST 35,683. O H26 traz a mesma linha.

tabela.afirmacao: Half a century later, the capital is still in Juneau.
tabela.fonte_diz: AS 44.06.010: 'The capital of the state is at the city of Juneau, Alaska.' De 1974 a 2026 são 52 anos, então 'half a century' é aproximação válida.

tabela.afirmacao: So what happened between that vote and the move that never came?
tabela.fonte_diz: A premissa se sustenta: a mudança nunca ocorreu (AS 44.06.010 vigente). A frase é pergunta retórica.

tabela.afirmacao: Official state returns put the yes vote at about 57 percent.
The answer comes down to one line that showed up on later ballots: the price.
tabela.fonte_diz: A cédula de 1978 trazia 'not more than $966,000,000' e a de 1982 'estimated to total $2,843,147,000'.

tabela.afirmacao: Its roads run about 43 miles north, to Cascade Point, and stop.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS 2018: 'The existing road system in Juneau currently extends approximately 43 miles to the north where Glacier Highway terminates at Cascade Point. No surface transportation facilities extend beyond Cascade Point.'

tabela.afirmacao: Every car, passenger and load of freight comes and goes by air or by sea.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'all freight, vehicle, and passenger movement to and from Juneau is by air or sea.'

tabela.afirmacao: One of them, Harris, chaired a committee pushing the move.
tabela.fonte_diz: Folheto de 1982, assinatura da declaração a favor da Medida 8: '—Frank W. Harris, Chairman, Capital Access Committee, Inc.' Reamer (ADN): 'pro-move Capital Access Committee chaired by Frank Harris'.

tabela.afirmacao: He made the case in the official voter pamphlet of 1982.
tabela.fonte_diz: Official Election Pamphlet 1982, 'Statement in Favor of Ballot Measure No. 8', assinada por Frank W. Harris.

tabela.afirmacao: Travel there, he wrote, "is so expensive and time consuming that few ordinary citizens are able to go there."
tabela.fonte_diz: Literal: 'Juneau is isolated, and travel to and from Juneau is so expensive and time consuming that few ordinary citizens are able to go there.' O trecho entre aspas bate letra a letra, e 'Travel there' está fora das aspas.

tabela.afirmacao: The city began as a gold camp in 1880.
tabela.fonte_diz: CBJ: 'On October 18, they staked a 160 acre town site on the beach where, the following month, they were joined by the first boatloads of prospectors'. O texto fala em 'the mining camp' em 1880.

tabela.afirmacao: In 1900, a federal law named Juneau the temporary seat of government, but the government stayed in Sitka, the old Russian capital.
tabela.fonte_diz: 31 Stat. 321 (6/6/1900): 'The temporary seat of government of said district is hereby established at Juneau: Provided, That the seat of government shall remain at Sitka until suitable grounds and buildings...' DOLWD: New Archangel (Sitka) 'became the capital and administrative center of Russian-America'.

tabela.afirmacao: The governor's office moved to Juneau in 1906.
tabela.fonte_diz: Relatório do governador Hoggatt (1/10/1906): 'on September 8 moved the executive office to Juneau.'

tabela.afirmacao: And the 1912 law creating the Territory of Alaska was plain: "the capital of the Territory of Alaska shall be at the city of Juneau, Alaska."
tabela.fonte_diz: 37 Stat. 512, Sec. 2 (24/8/1912): 'That the capital of the Territory of Alaska shall be at the city of Juneau, Alaska, and the seat of government shall be maintained there.' O trecho aspado é literal.

tabela.afirmacao: A railroad work camp became Anchorage in 1914.
tabela.fonte_diz: DOLWD: 'A railroad work camp at Ship Creek spawned the city of Anchorage in 1914.'

tabela.afirmacao: Around World War Two, military bases went up at Anchorage and Fairbanks.
tabela.fonte_diz: DOLWD: 'In 1939 and 1940, the Army built new bases in Anchorage (Fort Richardson) and Fairbanks (Ladd Field).'

tabela.afirmacao: The state labor department says the Anchorage and Fairbanks areas held roughly 15 percent of Alaskans in 1940.
tabela.fonte_diz: DOLWD: 'The Anchorage and Fairbanks areas, about 15 percent of the population in 1940, increased to 40 percent by 1950.'

tabela.afirmacao: By 1960, they held more than half.
tabela.fonte_diz: DOLWD: 'By 1960, those two cities and their surrounding areas would have more than half of Alaska's population'.

tabela.afirmacao: Voters rejected moving the capital in 1960 and 1962.
tabela.fonte_diz: H26: 08/09/1960 'Relocate the State Capital' 18,865 x 23,972. 11/06/1962: 26,452 x 32,325. O boletim oficial de 1962 dá 26,542 no 'sim'; em qualquer das versões, recusada.

tabela.afirmacao: In August 1974, they approved it.
tabela.fonte_diz: H26: 08/27/1974 'Relocate and Construct Capital' 46,659 x 35,683.

tabela.afirmacao: Anchorage's districts voted 80 percent yes.
tabela.fonte_diz: Boletim de 1974, p. 48, conferido na imagem. Os distritos 7 a 12, cujos precintos são todos 'Anchorage #' ou 'Gr Anch Boro #', somam FOR 27,064 e AGAINST 6,781: 79,96%.

tabela.afirmacao: The Southeast, around Juneau, voted about 94 percent no.
tabela.fonte_diz: Distritos 1 a 4 (bloco 'SOUTHEAST'): 116/3,763; 109/1,911; 148/2,119; 575/7,578. Soma: 948 a favor, 15,371 contra, ou seja 94,2% 'não'. O distrito 5 é SOUTHCENTRAL.

tabela.afirmacao: The 1974 law also set a rule: up to three candidate sites, none within 30 miles of Anchorage or Fairbanks.
tabela.fonte_diz: Folheto de 1976 (LAA): 'no more than three potential capital sites, none of which may be within a radius of 30 miles of the City of Anchorage or Fairbanks.'

tabela.afirmacao: As the attorney general summed it up in 1993, the premise was a planned capital away from the big cities.
tabela.fonte_diz: Parecer do AG Charles E. Cole (24/8/1993) sobre Boucher: 'on the premise that the new capital should be a planned capital not located in a relatively heavily urbanized area.'

tabela.afirmacao: That 1974 vote decided the capital would leave.
tabela.fonte_diz: Título oficial: 'Relocating and Constructing A New Capital', aprovado. O folheto de 1976 diz que o local mais votado 'shall be the site of the new capital city'.

tabela.afirmacao: In November 1976, voters picked the place.
tabela.fonte_diz: H28: 11/02/76 'Capital Site Selection Ballot Measure'.

tabela.afirmacao: The ballot offered three sites.
tabela.fonte_diz: H28: Larson Lake, Mount Yenlo, Willow. Folheto de 1976: 'The three sites presented on the ballot'.

tabela.afirmacao: The winner, with a little more than half the vote, lay near the town of Willow, in the Mat-Su Valley.
tabela.fonte_diz: Willow 56,219 de 105,558 (53,3%). O precinto Willow está no distrito 6, Mat-Su (boletim de 1974).

tabela.afirmacao: The site was about 70 road miles north of Anchorage, and five miles east of the town.
tabela.fonte_diz: Folheto de 1976: 'approximately 70 road miles north of Anchorage' e 'The town of Willow is five miles to the west' do local, logo o local fica 5 milhas a leste da vila.

tabela.afirmacao: In Fairbanks, a group wanted to know the price first.
tabela.fonte_diz: Folheto de 1978: FRANK 'organized in Fairbanks'; 'to insure the voter's right to know the full costs of the capital move before any significant additional money is spent'.

tabela.afirmacao: In early 1977, they organized the Frank committee, its name short for "Frustrated, Responsible Alaskans Needing Knowledge."
tabela.fonte_diz: Folheto de 1978: 'the FRANK (Frustrated, Responsible Alaskans Needing Knowledge) Committee which was organized in Fairbanks in early 1977'. Literal, com a vírgula. Em 1994 o comitê já se apresenta como 'Fiscally Responsible'.

tabela.afirmacao: Their initiative said the state could not spend money on the move until voters approved bonds covering its costs through 1992.
tabela.fonte_diz: Resumo do LAA: 'only after a majority ... have approved a general obligation bond proposition which includes all bondable costs of the relocation to the State through the year 1992.' 'Its costs' simplifica 'bondable costs', o que é aceitável.

tabela.afirmacao: The move's supporters answered the Frank initiative in the official 1978 voter pamphlet.
tabela.fonte_diz: 'Statement Against Ballot Proposition No. 3', assinada por 'FRANK HARRIS, Chairman, Taxpayers Capital Relocation Committee'.

tabela.afirmacao: "Its true purpose is to prohibit the move to Willow," their statement said.
tabela.fonte_diz: Literal: 'Its true purpose is to prohibit the move to Willow which the voters have authorized.' O corte antes de 'which' não altera o sentido.

tabela.afirmacao: In November 1978, the Frank initiative went to the voters.
tabela.fonte_diz: H26: 11/07/1978 'Full Bondable Costs of Relocating the Capital'.

tabela.afirmacao: On the same ballot sat the money to build: up to $966 million in bonds for the new capital, almost a billion dollars.
tabela.fonte_diz: Folheto de 1978, pergunta da cédula: 'bonds in the principal amount of not more than $966,000,000 for the purpose of paying the costs of capital improvements for the new state capital?'

tabela.afirmacao: The same voters made two choices.
tabela.fonte_diz: Boletim de 7/11/1978: Ballot Proposition #3 (FRANK) e Bonding Proposition #10 (New State Capital Construction Bond) na mesma eleição.

tabela.afirmacao: They passed the Frank initiative, with nearly 56 percent.
And they rejected the bonds, by almost three to one.
tabela.fonte_diz: 31,491 sim x 88,783 não, razão de 2,82:1. Reamer (ADN) dá os mesmos números.

tabela.afirmacao: In 1981, the legislature rewrote the rules.
tabela.fonte_diz: Resumo do LAA de 1982: 'The FRANK Initiative was amended by the Legislature in 1981'.

tabela.afirmacao: Instead, voters would get one last question in November 1982: could the state spend the money the move would take?
tabela.fonte_diz: Cédula: 'may the State of Alaska spend the money necessary (estimated to total $2,843,147,000) to accomplish relocation...?' O 'não' revogava tudo, por isso 'last' dentro daquele ciclo.

tabela.afirmacao: The ballot printed the state's estimate: about $2.8 billion, counted through 1994.
tabela.fonte_diz: 'TOTAL $2,843,147,000', com 'the anticipated relocation completion date of 1994'.

tabela.afirmacao: The estimate included nearly $590 million to compensate Juneau residents for the move.
tabela.fonte_diz: 'Indemnification of Juneau residents under AS 44.08 $589,323,000'.

tabela.afirmacao: It was winner-take-all.
tabela.fonte_diz: Resumo do LAA: se aprovada, 'the State shall relocate the capital'; se rejeitada, 'the Capital remains in Juneau and the following laws are repealed'. A página 100 Years of Alaska's Legislature chama o mecanismo de 'the winner takes all'.

tabela.afirmacao: Harris, the committee chair quoted earlier, called the figures inflated.
tabela.fonte_diz: Harris, 1982: 'Relocation need not and should not cost anything like the unrealistic, inflated estimates shown on the ballot measure.'

tabela.afirmacao: Jim Clark, against the move, reminded voters of the bonds they turned down in 1978.
tabela.fonte_diz: Jim Clark, Chairman, Alaska Committee: 'In that same year, the voters turned down a $966,000,000 bond issue to relocate the Capital.'

tabela.afirmacao: In 2026, he told Anchorage Daily News columnist David Reamer why.
tabela.fonte_diz: ADN, Reamer, publicado em 9/2/2026: 'As Stoops told me in a phone interview'. A lista de fontes registra 'Interview by David Reamer. February 2, 2026'.

tabela.afirmacao: "I decided to just make fun of the whole process and the amount of money they wanted to spend to move the capital and build in Willow."
tabela.fonte_diz: Literal: 'And I decided to just make fun of the whole process and the amount of money they wanted to spend to move the capital and build in Willow.' O 'And' inicial foi omitido, e o resto bate letra a letra.

tabela.afirmacao: Fannie's first ad priced 28 NFL teams and three domed stadiums at $800 million.
tabela.fonte_diz: 'the inaugural Football Fannie notice' (8/10/1982): '$20 million each for all 28 NFL teams comes to only $560 million... three domed stadiums for $80 million each. The whole package, 28 NFL Teams and 3 stadiums would only cost $800 million.' Conta: 560 + 240 = 800.

tabela.afirmacao: The ad called that about a quarter of the Willow price tag.
tabela.fonte_diz: 'Interestingly enough, this is only about one-fourth of the amount proposed to move the capital to Willow.' Conta: 800/2.843 = 28%, e a afirmação vem atribuída ao anúncio.

tabela.afirmacao: A Dittman Research poll in late September had the move ahead, 52 percent to 45.
tabela.fonte_diz: 'In late September 1982, Dittman Research ... Of the 527 respondents, 52% said they would probably vote in favor of the move versus 45% opposed.'

tabela.afirmacao: In November 1982, the no side won, with nearly 53 percent.
tabela.fonte_diz: Boletim por distrito: 91,049 sim x 102,083 não, ou 52,86%. O H29 e Reamer dão 91,249 no 'sim', ou 52,80%. As duas versões arredondam para 'nearly 53'.

tabela.afirmacao: Why voters said no is still argued.
tabela.fonte_diz: Stoops diz que a Fannie decidiu; Reamer diz 'At the very least ... a factor', 'At best ... perhaps the crucial variable'; Dittman não achava o preço relevante; Rae atribui ao custo. As versões divergem.

tabela.afirmacao: What they said no to is not.
tabela.fonte_diz: A pergunta estava impressa na cédula, com o custo de $2,843,147,000 (folheto de 1982).

tabela.afirmacao: Stoops says the satire decided it.
tabela.fonte_diz: Stoops: 'there's no way anyone could ever tell me that, that Football Fannie did not determine that election.'

tabela.afirmacao: Reamer calls it one factor, at the very least.
tabela.fonte_diz: 'At the very least, the NFL Access Committee was a factor in the failure of that capital move election.'

tabela.afirmacao: In 1990, state labor economist Brian Rae wrote that the expense "finally persuaded voters to reject the plans."
tabela.fonte_diz: Alaska Economic Trends, junho de 1990: 'The prohibitive expense of the capital move finally persuaded voters to reject the plans, and Juneau's economic future was secured'. A nota do autor diz 'Brian Rae is a labor economist', Research & Analysis, Department of Labor, 'based in Juneau'. Literal; o OCR mostra 'fmally' e 'plan s'.

tabela.afirmacao: Reamer adds that opponents spent more than a million dollars.
tabela.fonte_diz: 'Collectively, the anti-move groups spent over a million dollars in the lead-up to the 1982 election.'

tabela.afirmacao: By the ballot's own terms, the 1982 no vote also repealed every move law, from the 1974 initiative to the Frank initiative.
tabela.fonte_diz: Cédula: 'If a majority votes NO, laws and initiatives relating to capital relocation and indemnification are repealed.' O LAA lista 'the Capital Relocation Initiative; the FRANK Initiative as amended; the laws establishing the New Capital Site Planning Commission; and the Relocation Indemnification Act.'

tabela.afirmacao: The move came back in 1994.
tabela.fonte_diz: H26: 11/08/1994 93MCAP 'Relating to Changing the Capital to Wasilla'.

tabela.afirmacao: In the official election pamphlet, supporters said Wasilla was on the road system.
tabela.fonte_diz: Folheto de 1994, Statement of Support: 'Wasilla is an established community, centrally located on the road system between Fairbanks and Kenai Peninsula'.

tabela.afirmacao: Opponents recalled the 1982 estimate of about $2.8 billion.
tabela.fonte_diz: Statement in Opposition: 'Twelve years ago, the Capital Site Planning Commission estimated that it would cost $2,843,000,000 to move the capital.'

tabela.afirmacao: "This time," the statement against it said, "no price tag is attached."
tabela.fonte_diz: [reverificado na revisão final, troca F4] Folheto oficial de 1994, Medida 3, 'Change of Capital to Wasilla', 'STATEMENT IN OPPOSITION', p. B-24: 'This time, no price tag is attached.' (conferido na imagem). Antes: CONFIRMADA — Literal: 'This time, no price tag is attached.' Ressalva de atribuição: a declaração contrária não é assinada e está na 1ª pessoa do singular ('I believe', 'Please join me'), então 'they' é plural genérico (p. B-24, conferido na imagem).

tabela.afirmacao: In November 1994, nearly 55 percent voted no on Wasilla.
tabela.fonte_diz: Resultado de 1994: 'Ballot Measure No. 3 Capital Move Yes 96,398 45.3% No 116,277 54.7%'.

tabela.afirmacao: It lost without a price tag, so the price can't explain every defeat.
tabela.fonte_diz: O texto integral da 93MCAP tem só duas seções e nenhum custo (AG 1993; folheto de 1994). Mesmo assim, recusada por 54,7%.

tabela.afirmacao: The same ballot carried a second initiative: the right to know the cost first.
tabela.fonte_diz: H26: 11/08/1994 93COST 'Relating to Voters Rights to Know the Cost of Moving the Capital'.

tabela.afirmacao: It passed with about 77 percent.
tabela.fonte_diz: 'Ballot Measure No. 5 Capital Move Cost Yes 159,781 77.4% No 46,665 22.6%'.

tabela.afirmacao: That initiative revived the 1978 idea, and its wording is still law.
tabela.fonte_diz: As Seções 1 a 3 do texto de 1994 são idênticas às atuais AS 44.06.050, .055 e .060, conferido palavra por palavra. O comitê FRANK, em 1994: 'The FRANK Committee and Ballot Measure No. 5 are not new. In 1978...'

tabela.afirmacao: State money can move the capital or the legislature only after voters approve bonds for 12 years of costs.
tabela.fonte_diz: AS 44.06.055: 'only after a majority ... have approved a bond issue that includes all bondable costs ... over the twelve-year period following such approval.'

tabela.afirmacao: The rule covers the legislature too: lawmakers could move their sessions even with the capital still in Juneau.
tabela.fonte_diz: [reverificado na revisão final, troca F1] AS 44.06.055 ('relocate physically the capital or the legislature'); Medida 2 de 2002 (folheto, p. 128); HB 3, seções 3 e 16. Antes: NAO_ACHEI — A premissa se sustenta: a medida de 2002 e o HB 3 moveriam só o legislativo, com AS 44.06.010 intacto. Mas nenhuma fonte diz POR QUE a regra de 1994 inclui o legislativo. Nem a AS 44.06.050, nem o folheto de 1994 (LAA e FRANK) dão motivo. O 'because' entrou pela troca E8 (locução) nesta última etapa, sem evidência.

tabela.afirmacao: The law calls for a nine-member commission to tally the costs, including social, economic and environmental ones.
tabela.fonte_diz: [reverificado na revisão final, troca F3] AS 44.06.060 ('The legislature shall establish a commission composed of nine members'); AS 44.06.055 (custos sociais, econômicos e ambientais). Antes: CONFIRMADA — AS 44.06.060: 'The legislature shall establish a commission composed of nine members'. A .055 manda a comissão determinar custos que incluem 'the social, economic, and environmental costs'. Ressalva: a lei manda criar a comissão; não há comissão permanente, e o presente 'tallies' sugere que há.

tabela.afirmacao: The stated purpose is the people's "right to know."
tabela.fonte_diz: AS 44.06.050: 'to guarantee to the people their right to know and to approve in advance all costs'. O trecho aspado é literal.

tabela.afirmacao: Eight years later, voters rejected moving the legislative sessions to the Mat-Su Valley, by about two to one.
tabela.fonte_diz: 2002: 'MEASURE NO. 2 - LEGISLATIVE SESSION LOCATION ... YES 74650 32.77% NO 153127 67.23%', razão de 2,05:1. O folheto diz 'move all sessions of the state legislature to the Matanuska-Susitna (Mat-Su) Borough'. De 1994 a 2002 são 8 anos.

tabela.afirmacao: In 2025, a House bill to hold legislative sessions in Anchorage proposed repealing the whole cost law, for the capital as well as the legislature.
tabela.fonte_diz: HB 3, versão A (22/1/2025), 'HOLD LEGISLATIVE SESSIONS IN ANCHORAGE'. A Sec. 16 diz: 'AS 44.06.050, 44.06.055, and 44.06.060 are repealed.' Essas seções cobrem 'the capital or the legislature'.

tabela.afirmacao: As of September 2026, the bill hadn't left its first committee.
tabela.fonte_diz: BASIS, cópia local de 23/9/2026: 'Current Status (H) CRA Then STA, FIN', 'Status Date 01/22/2025'. Depois disso só há troca de patrocinador (13/2/2026) e novo coautor (18/3/2026). VOLÁTIL: o site ao vivo respondeu 403 (não contornei); reconferir na gravação.

tabela.afirmacao: Juneau's state senator, Jesse Kiehl, told KTOO in 2025: "It's a little bit like a zombie movie.
tabela.fonte_diz: KTOO, 13/6/2025 (Clarise Larson): 'Juneau Democratic Sen. Jesse Kiehl ... "It's a little bit like a zombie movie. It's never all the way dead," he said.' Literal.

tabela.afirmacao: It's never all the way dead."
tabela.fonte_diz: Mesma fala, literal: 'It's never all the way dead'.

tabela.afirmacao: The 2018 study for a Juneau road says travel limits feed the perception of an isolated capital.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'These restrictions also contribute to the perception held by many Alaska residents that the capital is isolated from the rest of the state.'

tabela.afirmacao: That leaves two corridors: the Taku River valley to the east, and Lynn Canal to the north.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'Because of geographical conditions, only two corridors are available ...: Lynn Canal and the Taku River Valley.'

tabela.afirmacao: British Columbia, the Canadian province next door, said in 1993 and 2003 it wasn't interested in the Taku.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'In 1993 ... B.C. indicated it did not support pursuit of this alternative.' E 'The October 2, 2003, response indicated that B.C. is not interested in the Taku River Valley Highway.'

tabela.afirmacao: In January 2000, Governor Tony Knowles picked the state's preferred option: a road up the east side of Lynn Canal.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'In January 2000, then-Governor Knowles declared Alternative 2, an East Lynn Canal Highway from Echo Cove to Skagway ..., the State's preferred alternative.'

tabela.afirmacao: Because of its high cost, he said, he wouldn't actively pursue it while he was in office.
tabela.fonte_diz: 9º Circuito (4/5/2011): 'stated that the alternative would not be actively pursued during his administration because of its high cost.' O motivo vem do tribunal; o FSEIS registra a decisão sem dar motivo.

tabela.afirmacao: That October, Juneau voters split almost evenly.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'In October 2000, Juneau voters were split on an advisory ballot question'.

tabela.afirmacao: Better ferries finished just 79 votes ahead of a road.
tabela.fonte_diz: '5,840 choosing enhanced ferry service and 5,761 choosing a road'. Diferença: 79.

tabela.afirmacao: Highway officials chose a version of that route in 2006.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'In April 2006, FHWA issued a Record of Decision ... stating that DOT&PF and FHWA selected Alternative 2B'.

tabela.afirmacao: The study counts 41 avalanche paths crossing it, and puts its cost at about $680 million.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'Alternative 2B crosses 41 avalanche paths' e 'Total final design and construction costs for Alternative 2B would be approximately $680.2 million'.

tabela.afirmacao: In 2009, a federal court threw out that choice.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'On February 13, 2009, the District Court vacated FHWA's ROD'.

tabela.afirmacao: The state first had to weigh better service with its existing ferries.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'failing to consider an alternative for improved ferry service using existing ferries and terminals'. O 9º Circuito manteve a decisão em 2011.

tabela.afirmacao: The study notes that for a decade, oil supplied about 90 percent of the state's unrestricted general fund revenue.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'between 2005 and 2014, oil revenues averaged 90 percent of Alaska's unrestricted general fund revenues (Knapp, 2015)'.

tabela.afirmacao: In just three years, oil prices lost more than three quarters of their value.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'from a high of more than $116 per barrel in February 2013 to a low of just over $26 per barrel in January 2016'. Queda de cerca de 77,6% em 35 meses.

tabela.afirmacao: In December 2016, Governor Bill Walker said he preferred what the study calls the No Action alternative: keep the ferries and build no road.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'press release dated December 15, 2016, announcing that he preferred Alternative 1 – No Action and that the JAI Project was being cut from the budget.'

tabela.afirmacao: The Juneau Assembly, the city council, still backed the road in January 2017, six to three.
tabela.fonte_diz: KTOO/CoastAlaska, 24/1/2017: 'a divided Assembly voted 6-3 to pass the resolution that affirmed its support for the road extension'. A votação foi na segunda-feira, 23/1.

tabela.afirmacao: "It would be a lot harder for me," she said, "if it were actually a road to Skagway or a road to Haines but it's a road to another ferry."
tabela.fonte_diz: Literal: 'It would be a lot harder for me if it were actually a road to Skagway or a road to Haines but it's a road to another ferry.' A interrupção com 'she said' não altera o texto.

tabela.afirmacao: The No Action alternative became final in June 2018.
tabela.fonte_diz: ROD assinado em 18/6/2018 por Sandra A. Garcia-Aline (FHWA): 'it is also my decision to select Alternative 1 – No Action'.

tabela.afirmacao: The 2018 decision pointed to the state's budget, and to a public fight over the road that had never been settled.
tabela.fonte_diz: ROD: 'Declining oil prices have caused the need for cuts to State budgets ... Controversy on the JAI Project is high among the public and disagreement remains among elected officials.'

tabela.afirmacao: The road north was never built, and Juneau's highway still stops about 43 miles north of town, at Cascade Point.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: rodovia de cerca de 43 milhas até Cascade Point. KTOO/KHNS de 20/3/2026: o estado adiou as obras do terminal de balsa em Cascade Point, e a rodovia continua terminando ali.

tabela.afirmacao: So what happened to that yes vote in 1974?
tabela.fonte_diz: Pergunta retórica. A premissa (o 'sim' de 1974) confere no boletim.

tabela.afirmacao: In 1974, the question was whether to move.
tabela.fonte_diz: 'Initiative #1 - Relocating and Constructing A New Capital'. O local e o custo ficaram para depois (folheto de 1976).

tabela.afirmacao: Voters said yes.
Both times a price went on the ballot, voters said no, though why is still debated.
tabela.fonte_diz: Os dois preços que foram à cédula: $966M em 1978 (31,491 x 88,783) e $2,843,147,000 em 1982 (91,049 x 102,083). As cédulas de 1994 e 2002 não traziam preço. A causa segue disputada (Stoops, Reamer, Dittman, Rae).

tabela.afirmacao: Since 1994, the law asks how much first.
tabela.fonte_diz: A 93COST foi aprovada em 1994, e o texto dela é hoje a AS 44.06.050–.060.

tabela.afirmacao: It just never came with a price voters would approve.
tabela.fonte_diz: Os dois preços foram recusados (1978, 1982). Nenhuma proposta com preço foi aprovada.

tabela.afirmacao: You can't drive to Juneau from the rest of the continent.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'Juneau is the largest community on the North American continent not connected to the continental highway system.'

tabela.afirmacao: The measure was a ballot initiative, a law that voters themselves put on the ballot.
tabela.fonte_diz: Boletim de 1974: 'Initiative #1'. O folheto de 1976 diz 'enacted by initiative in 1974'.

tabela.afirmacao: Juneau got the capital early, and the rest of Alaska grew up somewhere else.
tabela.fonte_diz: DOLWD: 'Before the war in the 1940 Census, Southeast was the most populous part of the territory'. A guerra 'secured the primacy of Anchorage and Fairbanks'.

tabela.afirmacao: Alaska's population, though, moved north.
tabela.fonte_diz: DOLWD: Anchorage e Fairbanks passam de cerca de 15% (1940) para mais da metade (1960).

tabela.afirmacao: The Alaska and Glenn highways tied Anchorage to the continent's roads.
tabela.fonte_diz: DOLWD: 'The Alaska Highway, built in 1942 ... connected Alaska with the lower 48 states and construction quickly followed of the Glenn Highway, which linked Anchorage to the national road system.'

tabela.afirmacao: Fairbanks split nearly even.
tabela.fonte_diz: Boletim de 1974, p. 48 (imagem): distrito 20 (precintos 'Fairbanks #'), 5,381 FOR x 5,243 AGAINST, ou 50,6%.

tabela.afirmacao: The state Supreme Court upheld the initiative that same year.
tabela.fonte_diz: AG 1993: 'In Boucher v. Engstrom, 528 P.2d 456 (Alaska 1974) ... the court upheld the initiative'.

tabela.afirmacao: A bond is money the state borrows and pays back over many years.
tabela.fonte_diz: Definição correta de título de obrigação geral ('general obligation bonds'), tipo usado na cédula de 1978.

tabela.afirmacao: Willow had a site, and no money approved to build on it.
tabela.fonte_diz: Local escolhido em 1976; títulos de construção recusados em 1978 (31,491 x 88,783).

tabela.afirmacao: There would be no bond vote this time.
tabela.fonte_diz: LAA 1982: a lei de 1981 exige 'a ballot proposition that includes the total cost', no lugar dos títulos. A Constituição, Art. XV § 26, fala em 'ballot proposition for the total cost'.

tabela.afirmacao: A yes vote meant building at Willow. A no vote meant Juneau stayed the capital.
tabela.fonte_diz: LAA: se adotada, 'the State shall relocate the capital'; se rejeitada, 'the Capital remains in Juneau'.

tabela.afirmacao: The pro-move side had a mascot, Access Annie. Lee Stoops, a legislative aide who lived in Juneau, answered with a rival: Football Fannie.
tabela.fonte_diz: Reamer: 'Lee Stoops, then an aide for state Sen. John Sackett ... a Juneau resident opposed to the capital move'; Fannie 'parodied Access Annie, the mascot for the pro-move Capital Access Committee'.

tabela.afirmacao: Before the vote, pollster Dave Dittman didn't think the price tag weighed that heavily.
tabela.fonte_diz: Reamer: 'He also did not believe the price tag was a sufficiently relevant factor in the outcome', dito junto com a divulgação da pesquisa, no dia seguinte ao primeiro anúncio (8/10/1982).

tabela.afirmacao: It was a printed price.
tabela.fonte_diz: A cédula de 1982 imprime '(estimated to total $2,843,147,000)' e as parcelas.

tabela.afirmacao: The new site was Wasilla, another Mat-Su Valley town, and the ballot carried no price.
tabela.fonte_diz: 'Shall the capital of Alaska be changed to Wasilla?' O texto tem duas seções, sem custo. O folheto de 1994 cita o 'beautiful Matanuska Valley'.

tabela.afirmacao: That measure would also have dropped the cost rule for moving the legislature.
tabela.fonte_diz: Cédula de 2002: 'The bill would repeal the requirements that before the state can spend money to move the legislature, the voters must be informed of the total costs ... and approve a bond issue'.

tabela.afirmacao: When a federal project could significantly change the environment, federal law requires an environmental impact statement, a study of what the project would change.
tabela.fonte_diz: [reverificado na revisão final, troca F2] 42 U.S.C. § 4332(2)(C) ('major Federal actions significantly affecting the quality of the human environment'); § 4336(b)(1); § 4336e. Ressalva leve: a lei diz 'major Federal action', mais amplo que 'federal project'. Antes: DIVERGE — 42 USC 4332(2)(C) exige o estudo para 'major Federal actions significantly affecting the quality of the human environment'. O gatilho é o efeito significativo, não o tamanho ou o dinheiro federal; muitas obras federais seguem com EA ou exclusão categórica. O dossiê não traz claim para esta frase.

tabela.afirmacao: Capital move supporters, it adds, often cite that.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'Capital move proponents often cite this as a reason to relocate the state's capital.'

tabela.afirmacao: Behind Juneau, an icefield straddles the border with British Columbia.
tabela.fonte_diz: Davies et al. 2024 (cópia local; a rede pediu login): 'Juneau Icefield (northern Coast Mountains) straddles the boundary between Alaska (USA) and British Columbia (Canada)'.

tabela.afirmacao: Lynn Canal is a long fjord between steep mountains, not a dug canal.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'Lynn Canal ... are all typical fjords occupying glacially sculpted valleys ... These mountains rise steeply from the water'.

tabela.afirmacao: Any road north would have to reach Haines or Skagway, at the top of that fjord. From there, the roads out cross into Canada and meet the Alaska Highway in the Yukon.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'Haines and Skagway, at the north end of Lynn Canal, are linked ... via the Alaska Highway. The Haines Highway connects Haines with the Alaska Highway at Haines Junction, Yukon Territory. The Klondike Highway links Skagway to the Alaska Highway near Whitehorse'.

tabela.afirmacao: With no such road, Juneau's official highway link is a ferry line: the Alaska Marine Highway, the state ferry system.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'The AMHS is the National Highway System link to Juneau, Haines, and Skagway.'

tabela.afirmacao: It stopped short of Haines and Skagway, so drivers would finish the trip on a ferry.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 2B 'from Echo Cove to a new ferry terminal 2 miles north of the Katzehin River, with ferry service connecting Katzehin to Haines and Skagway'.

tabela.afirmacao: Then the money ran short. That's the money that runs state government.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS: 'Alaska's State budget has been heavily reliant on oil taxes/royalties to fund State government'; 'major cuts to State capital and operating budgets'.

tabela.afirmacao: He cited the state's fiscal crisis.
tabela.fonte_diz: Walker, citado no FSEIS: 'I am very concerned with our current multi-billion dollar fiscal crisis and must prioritize the need for fiscal resolution'.

tabela.afirmacao: Assembly member Maria Gladziszewski voted no.
tabela.fonte_diz: 'Assembly members Jesse Kiehl and Loren Jones opposed the resolution. So did Assembly member Maria Gladziszewski.'

tabela.afirmacao: In the end, the road ran into a price too.
tabela.fonte_diz: FSEIS/ROD: 'the State cannot afford a high-cost, build transportation project in Lynn Canal at this time'. A controvérsia pública também entra como motivo.

tabela.afirmacao: For the capital to leave, voters would have to approve its price before state money could move it.
tabela.fonte_diz: AS 44.06.055, vigente. Vale só enquanto a lei não for revogada, e o HB 3 propõe revogá-la (já dito no texto).

tabela.afirmacao: What remained was choosing the place, and saying what it would cost.
tabela.fonte_diz: O local foi escolhido em 1976 (folheto de 1976). O custo ficou para a FRANK de 1978 e para a proposição de 1982.

tabela.afirmacao: Then it became how much.
tabela.fonte_diz: As cédulas de 1978 ($966M em títulos) e 1982 ($2,843,147,000) põem o custo em votação.

respostas.citacao: The road ran into the same rule. With oil prices falling, the state chose No Action.
respostas.motivo: Agora é 'The road ran into a cost problem of its own.' Cortei 'Someone would have to approve the bill.' e 'Neither bill... why the road ends there'. p6 termina no fato do ROD ('could not afford a high-cost project in Lynn Canal at that time', mec-01.24).

respostas.citacao: Voters didn't change their minds. They answered different questions.
respostas.motivo: Cortei as duas frases. Ficou só 'The question changed.', seguido de whether → how much.

respostas.citacao: For the capital to leave, voters would have to approve its price. They never have.
respostas.motivo: Consertei na estrutura. O veredito saiu de p5, que agora termina no fato de 2002, e foi para p7 como formulação final da regra. p7 não refaz a cronologia nem repete três a um, 53% ou 77%; paga o que p6 acrescentou (a estrada parou por custo) e a condição futura (HB 3).

respostas.citacao: The yes of 1974 was real. It just never came with a receipt.
respostas.motivo: O fecho agora é 'It just never came with a price voters would approve.', na palavra que a promessa plantou.

respostas.citacao: The record shows a pattern: the second time the bill went on the ballot, the bill lost.
respostas.motivo: Tirei 'bill' no sentido de conta de todo o roteiro; 'bill' só aparece em 'House bill', que é projeto de lei mesmo. O padrão foi para p7: 'Both times a price went on the ballot, voters said no, though why is still debated.'

respostas.citacao: Then came the price. In the spring of 1978, a twenty-eight-page, full-color insert reached nearly every Alaskan
respostas.motivo: 'Then came the price.' agora abre o parágrafo da cédula de novembro de 1978. Reordenei p3 em ordem cronológica: FRANK (início de 1977) → encarte (primavera de 1978) → folheto → votação. Não pus os US$ 3,5 bi da coluna para não disputar com os US$ 2,8 bi de 1982.

respostas.citacao: The state attorney general's summary gives the reason: a planned capital, away from a heavily urbanized area.
respostas.motivo: Agora: 'The state Supreme Court upheld the initiative that same year. As the attorney general later summed it up, the premise was a planned capital, away from a relatively heavily urbanized area.' (doc-23.2).

respostas.citacao: Frank Harris, of the Taxpayers Capital Relocation Committee, answered in the official 1978 voter pamphlet.

A ordem de p7 ficou assim: a estrada chega ao preço ("In the end, the road ran into a price too..."), vem a síntese e depois o fecho. Duas costuras foram necessárias. (1) Na síntese, cortei "They never have.", porque dizia o mesmo que a frase final ("never came with a price voters would approve"), e a M1 proíbe o fecho de repetir a síntese. (2) Em p5, a frase de 2025 ("proposed repealing that rule") agora vem logo depois de "the cost rule for moving the legislature", e o referente continua certo sem mexer em nada. Os ids das partes continuam os mesmos, e os bridges e a promessa_literal de p5, p6 e p7 foram atualizados.

respostas.citacao: Frank Harris chaired a committee pushing the move. / answered Frank / They passed Frank / from the 1974 initiative to Frank
respostas.motivo: Na fala, o homem virou "Harris": "One of them, Harris, chaired a committee pushing the move." O "One of them" é a costura mínima para apresentar o sobrenome sozinho, e o nome completo vai para a tela. O comitê virou "answered the Frank initiative", "They passed the Frank initiative" e "to the Frank initiative". Ficou um único "Frank" isolado, no ato de nomear o comitê ("a committee called Frank, short for..."), porque é ali que a sigla é definida. "The man you heard at the start" continua igual: a M3 não trata disso.

They had not said yes to the price." (p3); "So what happened to that yes vote in 1974?" (síntese, p7); "That yes vote was real." (fecho). respostas.citacao: Knowles / 1994 / Anchorage e Fairbanks / 77% / how much first / procurador-geral / weight / regra dos 12 anos / Taku / 2006
respostas.motivo: (1) Knowles: "picked the state's preferred option: a road up the east side of Lynn Canal". (2) 1994: "The move came back in 1994. The new site was Wasilla, another Mat-Su Valley town, and the ballot carried no price." (3) "the Anchorage and Fairbanks areas held roughly 15 percent of Alaskans in 1940". (4) Os 77% em frases curtas: "The same ballot carried a second initiative: the right to know the cost first. It passed with about 77 percent." A frase seguinte, "That initiative revived...", ficou igual, porque agora o referente é inequívoco. (5) "Since 1994, the law asks how much first." (6) "As the attorney general summed it up in 1993, the premise was a planned capital away from the big cities." (7) "weight" virou "population". (8) Regra dos 12 anos: entrou "The legislature could meet somewhere else, even with the capital still in Juneau." (doc-04.3, doc-20.1). Com isso, o "them" da frase seguinte apontaria para Juneau, então a costura mínima foi "A nine-member commission tallies the costs, including social, economic and environmental ones." (9) Taku: "British Columbia, the Canadian province next door, said...". (10) 2006: "It stopped short of Haines and Skagway, so drivers would finish the trip on a ferry." Conferência final: 1777 palavras, dentro da faixa de 1600–1850; frase média de 12,1 palavras; todos os excerpts saem literalmente da fala; todos os ids passaram no selecionar.mjs.
